column3: rationale

The arm64 port establishes its original address-profile constants, topic 0012 replaces the platform split with one scalable Darwin profile, and the same topic retunes the auxiliary allowance so vmalloc address space stops being the binding constraint on vmapped kernel stacks.
The arm64 UML port owns its architecture capabilities while topic 0020 exposes ACK's architecture-gated Android system-mapping sealing policy.
The arm64 port owns mmap policy while topic 0012 rejects guest mappings that cross the shared sparse native hole.
The arm64 port owns its relax primitive while topic 0013 turns an interruptible Darwin spin wait into a safe cooperative IPI boundary.
The arm64 signal port owns its restorer while topic 0012 moves the trampoline with the selected guest task ceiling.
The shared port establishes UML configuration while topic 0028 permits generic suspend to offline secondary vCPUs before the Darwin host enters sleep.

The shared port establishes UML build wiring, topic 0015 generates the arm64 kernel API headers required by ACK, and topic 0018 selects the freestanding arm64 Rust target for this Darwin-hosted kernel.
Topic 0010 introduces the Darwin user-network device while topic 0024 moves only its receive path onto NAPI so a sustained inbound stream cannot livelock the receiving CPU in interrupt context.
Topic 0010 adapts UBD host I/O to Darwin, while topic 0029 lets direct images batch discard ranges without changing upstream COW handling.

Darwin vhost-user transport support remains in topic 0010, the generic 64-bit DMA-mask correction stays independently reviewable and droppable as topic 0011, topic 0037 adds the negotiated standard shared-region transport used by host-visible Virtio-GPU blobs, and topic 0040 stops a device after backend EOF.
Topic 0010 owns the Darwin keyboard and absolute-pointer devices for every guest while topic 0023 reshapes only the pointer into the direct touchscreen Android's EventHub is able to classify.
The shared port establishes generic UML header selection while topic 0016 selects the generic SIMD-availability contract absent from ACK's UML headers.
The shared architecture topic owns pending-range marking while topic 0038 adds its caller-locked form and keeps user ranges exact instead of rounding them to a Darwin host page.
The shared task-layout contract remains in topic 0001 while topic 0012 selects the common scalable Darwin guest unmapped base.

The shared architecture topic declares the Darwin replay entry points, topic 0038 gives the locked replay a caller range and declares the access-granted hint, and topic 0039 completes or reports bounded kernel-range invalidation.

The shared architecture contract owns kernel-side host helpers, topic 0021 adds the IRQ-enabled cooperative timer checkpoint, the same topic generalizes its name for other safe in-kernel boundaries, and topic 0028 exposes the suspend-entry acknowledgement hook.

The shared host-service contract remains in topic 0001, topic 0022 adds the local IPI raise that arch_irq_work_raise() needs, topic 0025 adds the host call that releases a reported free range, and topic 0030 adds the virtual CPU's model name. Topic 0043 declares the bridge call that invalidates another mm's translated code.
The shared architecture topic declares the current-mm services while topic 0038 adds the access-granted query the Darwin fault dispatcher asks first.
The page-reclamation topic owns Darwin physical-range reporting while topic 0037 adds the guarded shared-memory aperture and its constant-time physical lookup.
The execution core owns Linux task entry while topic 0013 adapts its first activation to fixed Darwin vCPU carriers.
The MMU topic owns Darwin mm lifetime while topic 0038 removes the Darwin turnstile entry points that no longer have a caller.

The shared SKAS bootstrap owns CPU0 setup while topic 0013 installs Darwin's signal stack on the new CPU0 carrier. Topic 0038 takes the per-mm turnstile off the replay entry points and replays a granted fault with its 16 KiB neighbours.

The MMU topic makes user-page lookup safe across sibling page-table changes, topic 0021 adds a non-atomic PREEMPT_NONE quiescent boundary after all lookup locks are released, the same topic polls the cooperative timer before rescheduling there, and topic 0032 answers mmap-lock contention in a pagefault-disabled walk with an RCU page-table walk instead of a fault.
The SMP core owns the IPI vector table and dispatch while topic 0022 adds the irq-work vector and its arch_irq_work_raise() implementation.

The shared timer core owns Darwin timer delivery, topic 0021 exposes it through a kernel-register checkpoint for cooperative spin waits, and the same topic generalizes that checkpoint for safe retry and VMA-walk boundaries.

The MMU topic owns Darwin TLB synchronization and host invalidation, topic 0021 adds a quiescent boundary after each completed host VMA invalidation, and the same topic polls the cooperative timer there when logical IRQs are enabled. Topic 0038 lets walkers of one user mm run concurrently under the host invalidation epoch and adds the lockless access-granted hint. Topic 0039 bounds nested kernel-range invalidation and reports failure. Topic 0043 invalidates translated code after Linux writes a user page through its own mapping.
The MMU core owns guest fault dispatch while topic 0012 rejects faults that intersect the shared sparse native hole.

The execution core owns Darwin task-size setup, topic 0012 selects the common Apple task ceiling and scalable native hole, the same topic caps the auxiliary allowance and gives vmalloc the whole window rather than min(window, RAM), topic 0028 acknowledges suspension only after the platform enters its sleep boundary, and topic 0030 reports the emulator's CPU model name, and topic 0037 reserves the bounded guarded shared-memory GPA aperture inside that native layout.

The Darwin host implementation owns private service declarations, topic 0013 replaces per-task scheduler hooks with fixed-carrier lifetime hooks, the same topic adds the host-stop boundary, and topic 0031 declares the virtual-CPU ownership query a synchronous host fault is qualified against. Topic 0022 declares the pending-vector query the idle wait makes once a local vector exists.
The Darwin host implementation owns the entrypoint while topic 0013 keeps last-ditch signals from running Linux cleanup on an arbitrary carrier task.

The Darwin host service implementation owns the physical-memory backing, topic 0025 adds the regular-file range discard used by free-page reporting, and the same topic replaces only regular-file creation with the anonymous shared-memory diagnostic.
The Darwin host implementation owns host process services and installs the process-wide fault handlers, while topic 0031 claims the boot thread as their owner before those handlers exist.

The Darwin host implementation owns logical IRQ state, topic 0013 documents and pins its fixed-vCPU carrier ownership, and topic 0031 admits a synchronous host fault into the guest path only from the thread which owns the virtual CPU it would be attributed to.

The Darwin host implementation owns fault dispatch and scheduling; topic 0012 adds shared sparse guest-range validation, topic 0013 replaces per-task pthreads with stackful task contexts, the same topic stops those carriers at safe guest or idle boundaries, and topic 0030 advances the asserted bridge ABI identity. Topic 0036 delivers data-alignment exceptions through the versioned bridge. Topic 0038 replays a fault before Linux resolves it only when the PTE already grants the access. Topic 0042 sets the guest step bit around a ptrace single-step entry and reports the step as a trace trap. Topic 0043 advances the asserted bridge ABI identity.

The Darwin host implementation owns SMP and IPI transport, topic 0013 turns each bootstrap pthread into its permanent named vCPU carrier, the same topic services cross-CPU work while a carrier waits in kernel code, the same topic removes the once-guard from the interrupt-path current-vCPU read, topic 0021 services throttled cooperative timers after any IPI-driven migration, and the same topic updates that call to the generalized safe-kernel checkpoint, and topic 0022 publishes a self-directed vector so a local irq-work raise reaches that same cooperative drain. Topic 0031 reports which virtual CPU, if any, the running host thread carries.
The Darwin host implementation owns host start-up probing while topic 0030 forwards the emulator's CPU model name.

The Darwin host implementation owns cooperative idle waits while topic 0013 adds the per-run stop descriptor to the wait set. Topic 0022 polls instead of blocking while a vector is pending, because its local vector has no wake edge.

The Darwin bridge topic owns generated ABI declarations, topic 0012 carries the selected signal-restorer address, topic 0013 adds the allocation-free active-stop event, and topic 0030 advances the identity for the CPU model name. Topic 0036 delivers data-alignment exceptions through the versioned bridge. Topic 0043 advances the identity for code invalidation by generation.

The Darwin bridge topic owns generated ABI identity while topics 0012, 0013 and 0030 advance it for the signal-restorer, host-stop and CPU-identity contracts. Topic 0036 delivers data-alignment exceptions through the versioned bridge. Topic 0043 advances the identity for code invalidation by generation.
The Darwin bridge topic owns the CPU entry points while topic 0030 adds the model-name query.
The Darwin bridge topic owns host-service declarations while topic 0013 exposes the per-run stop descriptor and predicate.
The Darwin bridge owns memory declarations while topic 0043 adds code invalidation for another mm's generation.
The Linux host implementation owns SMP and IPI transport while topic 0022 adds the local raise, which its queued self-directed signal already delivers correctly.
